chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, hearts have periods of forward movement and backward movement. When they move forward, engage them in optional acts of worship, and when they move backward, restrict them to obligatory acts only.

key_terms.إِدْبَار: Backward movement or turning away (of the heart from worship)
key_terms.إِقْبَال: Forward movement or inclination (of the heart towards worship)
key_terms.النَّوَافِل: Optional acts of worship (supererogatory prayers, etc.)
key_terms.الْفَرَائِض: Obligatory duties (such as the five daily prayers)

ai.seo_question: How to balance obligatory and optional worship based on spiritual state?
ai.summary: This maxim from Nahj al-Balagha reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of *tadrij* (gradualism) in spiritual practice, warning against the common error of overextending oneself during periods of low energy (*idbar*), which can lead to burnout or neglect of core duties. By prioritizing the *fara'id* when the heart is distracted, the believer ensures the foundation of faith remains intact, while leveraging peaks of devotion (*iqbal*) for voluntary acts that elevate one's spiritual station.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 312. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

Sometimes the hearts move forward and sometimes they move backward. When they move forward get them to perform the optionals (as well), but when they move backward keep them confined to obligatories only.
